harbor.practice: Harbor knew the right policy but formatted extractions inconsistently, so it got a small SFT; missing-policy failures were fixed in retrieval instead.
harbor.failure: Training around an ingestion or authorisation bug that should be fixed in code.

harbor.practice: Harbor's extraction guideline says a missing effective date is null, never inferred; two annotators label a shared sample and resolve disagreements before scaling up.
harbor.failure: Scaling annotation before the guideline produces agreement, which trains the model to be confidently inconsistent.

harbor.practice: Harbor's format adapter is LoRA rank 16 on attention and MLP layers of an 8B model: about 42M trainable parameters, an 84 MB adapter file.
harbor.failure: Assuming few trainable parameters means low compute; the frozen base still runs forward and backward.

harbor.practice: Harbor trained on 3,000 extraction records including 600 with absent fields, and tests on policy families it never saw in training.
harbor.failure: Assuming a trained tool-call format authorises execution or guarantees the chosen action is right.

harbor.practice: Harbor's embedding fine-tune uses adjudicated query, positive and hard-negative triples, and is judged by Recall@20 on real queries and then by answer quality.
harbor.failure: Mining hard negatives without checking them; some are valid answers, and the model learns to reject good evidence.

harbor.practice: Harbor's adapter improved field accuracy but began filling missing IDs with plausible values; that blocked release despite a higher average score.
harbor.failure: Treating a few passed privacy probes as proof that no training data can be extracted.

harbor.practice: Harbor's adapter-r431 is registered with its exact base revision, tokenizer, dataset manifest, schema and evaluation suite; deploying it on another base revision requires re-testing.
harbor.failure: Recording a model by name without an immutable revision.
